Area.evidence_source: By engaging the everyday experiences of community members, this study found multiple explanations for suicidal behavior in the Cowichan Tribes. At the individual level, participants described experiences such as separation from families, which led to thwarted belongingness and extreme loneliness; domestic violence, which resulted in a perceived sense of burdensomeness; and family history of suicidal behavior, which facilitated the capacity to enact lethal self-harm. Suicide in Cowichan was also associated with mental health conditions and substance abuse, as in other Indigenous communities in North America (LeMaster, Beals, Novins, & Manson, 2004).
